claims.claim: Taxation is source-based today, so foreign dividends and interest are untaxed

sources.name: PwC: Costa Rica, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 30 June 2026. "Income taxes on individuals in Costa Rica are levied on local income irrespective of nationality and resident status." Foreign-source dividends and interest are not addressed; no worldwide-income bill is mentioned.

sources.name: KPMG Costa Rica: Newsflash, 29 September 2026
sources.says: Filed 22 September 2026 as expediente 25.796; "Se extiende el gravamen de las rentas pasivas de fuente extranjera a residentes en Costa Rica en general"; "se plantea un esquema de deducción y no de acreditación"; no exemptions mentioned; still in the legislative process. No rate given.

claims.note: PwC taxes "local income" and does not name foreign dividends; KPMG's note that the bill would "extend" the tax on foreign passive income to residents in general confirms it is not taxed today. Tax score 5 stays (today's rule).

sources.says: Costa Rica (last reviewed 30 June 2026): "Costa Rica does not have an inheritance tax." "Costa Rica does not have a gift tax." Panama (last reviewed 04 August 2026): NA | NA. Dominican Republic (last reviewed 25 August 2026): 3 | 27. Belize is not listed.

claims.claim: There is no US estate treaty

sources.name: IRS: Estate & gift tax treaties (international)
sources.says: The table has 15 countries (see us-estate-treaty-list); none of the 37 countries named in this claim is among them.

claims.claim: US estate tax applies to the worldwide estate above the $15M exemption (2026)

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.

sources.says: Published October 23, 2026. sources.name: Your Tax Base: Charles Schwab for expats
sources.says: Dated October 23, 2026 (country check that day). Rows "Costa Rica | Yes" and "Panama | Yes" (both among the 51 accepted); "Dominican Republic | No"; Belize is absent from the table and the 51-country list, and residents of the other countries saw "Schwab currently cannot open accounts for residents of your country/region." claims.claim: Rentista needs stable income of at least $2,500/month for 2 years, with no compulsory deposit on the official checklist checked in September 2026

sources.name: CRIE: Costa Rica Rentista residency deposit requirements
sources.says: Dated October 4, 2026. DGME requires "stable and permanent income of at least US$2,500 per month" for at least two years; "The published checklist does not set out a compulsory US$60,000 deposit for every applicant" (checked September 6, 2026); US$60,000 is 24 × US$2,500. Graphic: pensionado US$1,000/month, investor US$150,000.

sources.name: Rio Times: Residency in Costa Rica for foreigners 2026
sources.says: Published 20 September 2026, modified 8 November 2026. Rentista: "US$2,500 a month, guaranteed for at least two years"; "Investment income, an annuity or savings point to rentista", but whether brokerage income counts as evidence is not addressed. Pensionado: "at least US$1,000 a month". Investor: Ley 9996's US$150,000 window closed; "Anyone filing now should plan on US$200,000", figure unconfirmed. Processing: three months by rule, but the ombudsman "found a backlog of about one year". "Every temporary resident must join the Caja"; "The health insurance rate totals 12% of declared income" (February 2025 report).

claims.note: Check for a bill: no 2026 bill changing the rentista or pensionado amounts was found. Visa score 4 stays.
